title: 一枚にできない景色
paragraphs: A city art project invited residents to photograph the same square at different hours. The organizers expected a collection of similar views with changing light. Instead, the pictures revealed activities that rarely appeared together: delivery workers at dawn, children after school, and cleaners late at night. Some residents had never realized how many groups depended on the square.
同じ広場を時刻別に撮る企画は光の変化を予想したが、早朝配送、放課後の子、深夜清掃など共存しにくい活動を明らかにした。

The exhibition placed the photographs in time order without selecting one as the most authentic view. A quiet morning picture did not cancel the truth of a busy evening one. Each showed a limited but meaningful part of the place. Visitors began adding notes about activities missing from the collection, including routines too ordinary for anyone to photograph.
時間順の展示で一枚を最も本物とはせず、静かな朝も混む夜を否定しないと示した。各写真は限定的だが意味があり、来場者は撮るほどでない日常など欠けた活動を追記した。

The project did not produce a complete portrait. It changed the question from Which image represents our square? to What does each image help us notice, and what remains outside it? The organizers learned that combining partial views could reveal more than searching for a single perfect picture, provided that the gaps were treated as invitations to keep looking rather than quietly ignored.
完全な肖像を作るのでなく、代表一枚を探す問いから各写真が見せるものと外側への問いに変わった。不足を無視せず見続ける招きとすれば、部分視点の組合せは完璧一枚の探索より多くを示すと学んだ。
questions: 部分的な視点を重ねて場所を知る
一枚だけが示す唯一の真実
広場を夜間閉鎖する方法
写真から日常を取り除く
複数視点と不足への注意が主題。
予想と違って現れたものは？
集団の使い方が見えた。
syntax: Each showed a limited but meaningful part of the place.
a limited but meaningful part of the place
各写真は限定的でも意味ある場所の一部を示した。
Eachは各写真。butで限界と価値を両立して述べる。

title: 空欄のある作品集
paragraphs: A young designer prepared a portfolio for an interview. She filled it with polished images and removed every sketch showing uncertainty. A friend who reviewed it admired the results but could not understand how the designer had reached them. Several projects looked as if they had appeared fully formed.
若いデザイナーは面接作品集から迷いの下絵を全て消し整った画像だけにした。友人は結果を褒めても到達過程が不明だった。

The designer restored a few early drawings and wrote short explanations of decisions she had changed. One page showed a rejected layout beside the final version, with a note explaining why a user had found the first one confusing. The portfolio became less visually uniform, but made her thinking easier to follow.
初期図と変更理由を戻し、分かりにくいと利用者に言われた没案も完成版横に示すと見た目の統一は減っても思考を追いやすくなった。

At the interview, the discussion focused on how she responded to evidence and worked through problems. She did not suggest that unfinished work should replace finished results. Both were necessary for the story she wanted to tell. A perfect surface could demonstrate skill, while selected traces of revision could demonstrate judgment. The experience changed how she documented later projects: she kept records of important choices instead of trying to reconstruct a convincing process after the work was already complete.
面接は証拠への応答と問題解決が中心になった。未完成で完成を置き換えず、整った表面は技能、選んだ改訂跡は判断を示すので両方必要だった。以後は完成後に説得的過程を再構成せず重要選択をその都度記録した。
questions: 完成品と判断の過程を共に示す
下絵だけで全て代用する
面接で失敗を必ず隠す
作品の見た目は全て無意味
重要な選択を進行中に残す
完成品を一切保存しない
後で再構成しないため。
syntax: The portfolio became less visually uniform, but made her thinking easier to follow.
made her thinking easier to follow
作品集の視覚的統一は減ったが思考は追いやすくなった。
make O CのOはher thinking、Cはeasier to follow。

title: きれいな表示と使える表示
paragraphs: A train station replaced an old information board with a large digital screen. The new design showed beautiful photographs between departure notices. In a publicity picture, the entrance looked modern and uncluttered. Yet several passengers said they found it harder to check a platform number quickly.
駅の新デジタル案内は発車情報の間に美しい写真を映し宣伝では近代的で整然としたが、番線を確認しにくい声があった。

The designers observed people during a busy evening. Photographs stayed on screen longer than the information some travelers needed. Small text also became difficult to read from behind a crowd. The screen was attractive when photographed from an empty hall, but less effective from the positions passengers actually occupied.
混雑時に観察すると写真時間が長く人越しに小字が読みにくかった。無人ホールの撮影位置では美しくても実際の乗客位置で有効でなかった。

The station changed the display cycle and kept essential departures visible continuously. Photographs moved to a separate part of the entrance. The result looked less dramatic in advertising, but served its main purpose better. Staff continued testing the board from different distances and heights. They learned that a public display should be judged not only as an image in a presentation, but as information people must find while carrying bags, moving through crowds, and deciding where to go under time pressure.
重要発車情報を常時表示し写真は別区域へ移すと広告的迫力は減っても役割は改善した。距離や高さを変え試し続け、荷物、混雑、時間圧力の中で探す情報として評価すべきと学んだ。
questions: 見栄えと実際の利用場面の差
写真を永久に禁止する駅
広告のためだけの乗客
現場の使いやすさが主題。
写真が長く小字も見づらい
写真の後にしか出さない
必要情報への即時アクセス。
syntax: The result looked less dramatic in advertising, but served its main purpose better.
広告での迫力は減ったが主目的はよりよく果たした。
look＋形容詞で見え方。butで見栄えと機能を対比する。

title: 助ける前に聞くこと
paragraphs: During a charity project, students planned to send books to a small community center. They collected many old textbooks and were proud of the growing pile. Before arranging delivery, their adviser suggested contacting the center about what its readers actually needed. The students expected a simple expression of thanks.
慈善活動の学生は古い教科書の山を誇ったが、発送前に必要を聞くよう顧問に勧められ、礼だけを予想した。

The center's coordinator explained that most visitors were adults learning to read more confidently. Short practical guides with clear print would be more useful than advanced school textbooks. Storage space was limited, and sorting unsuitable donations would take time away from teaching. The coordinator welcomed support, but wanted it to respond to local priorities.
施設利用者は読む力を伸ばす成人が多く、難しい教科書より明瞭な短い実用書が有用。保管と不適品分類は教える時間を奪うので地域の優先に応じた支援を求めた。

The students changed their plan. They sorted the original collection, found appropriate homes for some books, and used a small fundraiser to purchase materials requested by the center. Their final report described this change rather than hiding it. They learned that generosity involved more than giving away what was available. Listening could make the difference between a gift that impressed the giver and assistance that made the receiver's work easier.
学生は仕分けし一部を別の受取先へ、募金で希望資料を購入した。変更も隠さず報告。寛大さは手元の物を渡す以上で、贈り手の満足と受け手を助ける支援の違いは聴くことにあると学んだ。
questions: 相手の必要を聞いて支援を考える
寄付は量だけで評価する
教科書を全て捨てる活動
感謝だけを求める施設
施設は具体需要を説明。
Short practical guides with clear print
最終報告は変更をどう扱ったか。
syntax: Storage space was limited, and sorting unsuitable donations would take time away from teaching.
sorting unsuitable donations would take time away from teaching
保管場所は限られ、不適な寄付の分類は教育時間を奪うだろう。
後半の主語は動名詞句sorting unsuitable donations。

title: 遅い返事の意味
paragraphs: A student named Daniel worked with an overseas partner on a shared history project. Daniel sent ideas through a chat app and expected quick replies because messages appeared instantly. When his partner did not answer until the following day, he worried that she was losing interest. He began sending repeated reminders.
ダニエルは海外との歴史企画で即着チャットに即答を期待し、翌日まで返らないと関心低下を恐れ何度も催促した。

During their first video meeting, he learned that she shared one computer with her siblings and usually worked after dinner. The time difference also meant that his afternoon messages arrived during her school day. She had been reading carefully and gathering evidence before replying, not ignoring the project.
ビデオ会議で相手は兄弟と一台を共有し夕食後に作業、時差でこちらの午後は相手の授業中と分かった。無視でなく資料を調べて丁寧に返していた。

They agreed on two scheduled check-ins each week and used a shared document for questions that could wait. Daniel stopped judging commitment by response speed alone. The technology had made distance less visible, but had not removed different schedules, resources, and habits. Their cooperation improved when they explained these conditions to each other. Fast communication was still useful for urgent changes, while slower replies sometimes contained the thought that made the joint work stronger.
週二回の確認と待てる問い用の共有文書に合意し、返答速度だけで関与を測るのをやめた。技術は距離を見えにくくしても生活や資源差をなくさない。条件を説明すると協働が改善し、緊急時の速さと遅い熟考の両方が役立った。
questions: 返答の速さだけでは測れない協力
即答だけが関心の証拠
歴史調査をやめる理由
機器共有と生活時刻の違い
企画への無関心が確定
メッセージが届かない
shared one computer with her siblings
週二回確認と共有文書
急ぎも必ず一か月待つ
syntax: The technology had made distance less visible, but had not removed different schedules, resources, and habits.
技術は距離を見えにくくしたが予定や資源、習慣の違いは消していなかった。
make O Cの形。butの後は主語を省略し対比する。
vocabulary: 関与・責任を持つ姿勢

title: 発見を生む分類箱
paragraphs: A natural history club collected photographs of leaves around its school. Members first sorted them into green, yellow, and brown folders. The arrangement looked clear, but comparing the photographs was difficult because leaves from the same tree appeared in different folders as the season changed.
自然史部は葉写真を緑黄茶に分けたが同じ木でも季節で別箱になり比較しにくかった。

A teacher asked the club to consider what question its classification was meant to answer. Color was useful for studying seasonal changes, but shape and location might be better for comparing different trees. No single arrangement was automatically correct for every purpose. The club kept the original files and created several views using labels rather than moving each photograph permanently.
先生は分類が答える問いを尋ね、色は季節、形や位置は木の比較に有用と示した。全目的に唯一正解でないので原ファイルを保持しラベルで複数の見方を作った。

Students could now examine one tree across months or compare shapes on the same date. They also recorded uncertain identifications instead of forcing every image into a definite category. Their project showed that classification did more than tidy a collection. It made some relationships easier to see while hiding others. Choosing categories carefully, and being willing to revise them, became part of the investigation rather than a simple task completed before the real learning began.
一木の月別と同日の形の比較ができ、不確かな同定も無理に確定しなかった。分類は整理以上にある関係を見せ他を隠す。目的に合わせ見直すこと自体が探究で、学び前に終える雑務ではなかった。
questions: 分類は問いに応じて見方を変える
一つの正しい箱が全てを示す
葉の色を覚えるだけの学習
不明な物は全て捨てる
what question its classification was meant to answer
同じ木の写真が季節で分散
月を一度も記録できない
different folders as the season changed
原本を残しラベルで複数表示
syntax: It made some relationships easier to see while hiding others.
分類は一部の関係を見やすくしつつ他を隠した。
make O Cとwhile＋分詞の対照。othersは他の関係。

title: 声に出して読む理由
paragraphs: At a writing workshop, participants were asked to read their drafts aloud to a partner. A student called Bea objected that written essays were meant to be read silently. She believed that correcting spelling and grammar on a screen was enough to make her argument clear.
作文講座で下書きを音読するよう言われ、ベアは黙読用だから画面の文法綴り修正で十分と反対した。

When she read her own essay, however, she stopped twice because sentences contained too many qualifications. Her partner understood individual words but could not remember which claim the examples supported. Hearing the draft made a structural problem more noticeable than it had been during silent revision.
実際に読むと限定表現が多すぎ二度止まり、相手は単語は分かっても例がどの主張を支えるか忘れた。黙って直す時より構造問題が明確になった。

Bea shortened one sentence, moved an example, and added a phrase explaining the connection between two paragraphs. She still checked grammar afterward. Reading aloud had not replaced other forms of editing; it had provided a different route to noticing difficulties. The instructor explained that no method would expose every weakness in every text. Trying more than one way of reviewing could help a writer encounter her own work as a reader might, rather than seeing only the intentions she already knew.
文を短縮し例を移し段落間のつながりを足してから文法も確認。音読は他の編集の代わりでなく別の気づき方だった。万能法はなく複数の見直しで、既知の意図だけでなく読者のように自作と出会えると講師は説明した。
questions: 異なる見直し方で文章の問題に気づく
音読だけで文法確認は不要
綴りだけで論証は完成する
a different route to noticing difficulties
文の限定過多と例の支える主張の不明確さ
万能法はなく複数法が役立つ
一方法が全弱点を必ず発見
no method would expose every weakness
syntax: Reading aloud had not replaced other forms of editing
音読は他の編集方法を置き換えなかった。
動名詞句が主語。過去完了で修正過程を振り返る。

title: 競争しない学習記録
paragraphs: A language club introduced a weekly chart showing how many minutes each member had studied. The organizer hoped public numbers would encourage regular practice. Some students enjoyed moving upward on the list, but others stopped posting. One member who read slowly spent a long time on a short text and felt that the chart said little about what she had understood.
語学部の週学習分数ランキングは習慣を促したが、楽しむ人の一方で投稿をやめる人もいた。遅く丁寧に読む人には理解が数字に映らなかった。

The club discussed what its records were supposed to support. Minutes could help someone notice a habit, yet did not measure every kind of learning. A difficult conversation, a careful correction, and an easy review could all occupy the same amount of time while serving different purposes.
分数は習慣把握にはよくても学び全体を測らず、難しい会話、訂正、易しい復習は同時間でも目的が違うと話した。

The club replaced the ranking with private time records and a shared board for short reflections. Members described one thing they had noticed or wanted to try next. The new system still encouraged consistency, but no longer treated a larger number as automatic evidence of greater progress. Students learned to use a measurement as a tool for reflection rather than allowing it to become the entire definition of success.
順位を個人時間記録と共有の短い振り返りへ替え、気づきや次の試みを書いた。継続は促すが大きい数字を自動的な進歩とせず、尺度を成功の全定義でなく内省の道具として使うと学んだ。
questions: 記録を学びの振り返りに使う
分数だけが能力を示す
競争なしでは継続できない
丁寧な理解が数字だけに表れない
分数が一度も表示されない
共有掲示が存在しない
新たに共有したものは？
syntax: Minutes could help someone notice a habit, yet did not measure every kind of learning.
did not measure every kind of learning
分数は習慣の気づきを助けてもあらゆる学びを測れなかった。
help 人 動詞原形。yetで有用性と限界を対比する。

title: 見学路の小さな窓
paragraphs: A factory offered tours along a glass corridor above its production floor. Visitors could watch machines moving quickly and products leaving the line. Many described the process as almost completely automatic. A worker who read the comments felt that the tour had made part of the work invisible.
工場のガラス廊下から機械と出荷を見た客はほぼ自動と評したが、働き手は一部が不可視と感じた。

Before the line started, technicians adjusted equipment and checked materials. During operation, experienced workers listened for unusual sounds and inspected small changes in the products. These activities were difficult to notice from the corridor, especially during a short visit when nothing went wrong. The smooth movement that impressed visitors depended partly on attention they could not see.
始動前の調整や材料点検、運転中の異音や小変化への熟練の注意は、問題のない短時間見学では見えにくい。滑らかさは見えない注意にも依存した。

The factory added a display explaining preparation and judgment behind the visible process. A short interview with a worker described a time when an early warning prevented a longer interruption. The machines remained central to the tour, but were no longer presented as acting without human skill. Visitors gained a fuller account of production, and workers could recognize more of their own contribution in the story being told about their workplace.
準備と判断の展示、早い警告が長い停止を防いだ聞き取りを追加。機械は中心に残すが人の技能なしとはせず、客には全体像、働き手には自らの貢献が見える職場の物語になった。
questions: 自動化の表面を支える人の技能
人のいない工場の完成
機械を全て撤去する見学
生産を止めるための広告
見えにくい判断を可視化。
廊下から見えにくい仕事は？
事前調整や異常への注意
改訂した見学の説明は？
機械と人の技能の両方
syntax: The smooth movement that impressed visitors depended partly on attention they could not see.
The smooth movement that impressed visitors
partly on attention they could not see
客を感心させる滑らかな動作は見えない注意にも依存した。
that節がmovementを修飾し、attentionの後は目的格関係詞を省略している。

title: 友達のための説明図
paragraphs: A student named Rosa understood a science topic after watching an animation. She decided to make a diagram for a friend who had missed the lesson. At first, she copied the animation's main shapes and added the same labels. The result looked accurate, but her friend asked why one stage led to the next.
ローザは科学の動画で分かったと思い欠席した友へ図を作った。形とラベルを写すと正確に見えても段階がつながる理由を問われた。

Rosa discovered that recognizing the pictures had not meant she could explain every connection. She returned to the lesson notes and marked the steps where her own understanding was uncertain. Then she redrew the diagram with arrows carrying short explanations rather than merely showing direction. Her friend asked further questions, and both students revised one part together.
絵の認識は接続の説明と違うと気づきノートで曖昧箇所を調べ、矢印に方向だけでなく理由も書き、友の問いで一部を共同修正した。

The final diagram was useful, but the larger benefit had come during its creation. Preparing to teach someone else had exposed gaps that silent review had left hidden. Rosa did not conclude that every student should become an expert tutor. She learned that attempting a clear explanation, and welcoming questions when it failed, could turn confidence in familiar images into a more careful understanding of the ideas those images represented.
完成図より制作中の学びが大きかった。教える準備が黙読では隠れた穴を露出した。全員が専門講師になるのでなく、説明を試し失敗時の質問を歓迎すれば、見慣れた絵への自信を考えの丁寧な理解へ変えられると学んだ。
questions: 説明を作ることで理解の穴を見つける
絵を写せば必ず全て理解
全学生を専門講師にする
制作と問いで理解を深める。
why one stage led to the next
syntax: Preparing to teach someone else had exposed gaps that silent review had left hidden.
gaps that silent review had left hidden
他人へ教える準備が黙って復習した際に隠れていた穴を示した。
動名詞句が主語。left hiddenはOを隠れたままにしたという構造。
